title: Lady Six Sky (Ix Wak Chan Ajaw) of Naranjo
summary: Lady Six Sky came from Dos Pilas to the Maya city of Naranjo in AD 682, where she ruled or acted as regent for her son until he took the throne in 693. Monuments such as Stela 24 record her; some scholars think her influence lasted to her death in 741.

uncertainty.note: Regency dates 682–693 appear in the SMU thesis and the Penn Museum article; AD 741 is the death date in the Calvin chart. The thesis calls the late influence possible.

as_recorded.calendar: AD (Long Count converted by the source)

as_recorded.value: from 682 to 693 A.D. as regent for her son

where.historical_name: Naranjo, Classic Maya kingdom in the Petén lowlands

importance.justification: Rare Classic Maya woman ruler who restored a lineage and left several monuments.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the arrival year 682 (read as the start date in two scholarly sources, not from Stela 24 itself) and the scale of her rule after 693. The name reading is still contested, hence the common name Lady Six Sky; father (Bajlaj Chan K’awiil of Dos Pilas) comes from the Calvin chart only. Do not confuse with the Lady Six Sky of Yaxchilan.
